cards.text: Meanwhile, Rehoboam son of Solomon reigns in Judah. He's forty-one when he becomes king, and he reigns seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the LORD chose to put His Name. His mother's name is Naamah the Ammonite.

cards.question: Under Rehoboam, how does Judah live in the LORD's sight?

answers.text: They provoke Him more than their fathers did
They serve Him more faithfully than their fathers
They tear down every idol in the land

cards.text: They build high places, sacred pillars and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree. EVERY green tree, baker, and there are even male shrine prostitutes in the land.

cards.question: True or false: Judah's worship under Rehoboam looks nothing like the nations the LORD drove out before Israel.

cards.text: In the fifth year of Rehoboam's reign, Shishak king of Egypt attacks Jerusalem. No knock, no text, no heads-up in the group chat.

cards.question: What does Shishak king of Egypt seize in Jerusalem?

answers.text: The treasures of the temple and the palace
The young men of Jerusalem as captives

cards.question: Shishak takes everything, even all the gold ___ that Solomon had made.

cards.text: So King Rehoboam has new shields made to put in their place. Gotta give the guards SOMETHING to carry.

cards.question: To replace Solomon's gold shields, King Rehoboam makes shields of ___.

cards.text: He puts them in the care of the captains of the guard at the entrance to the royal palace. Gold out, bronze in, like swapping your good cookie sheet for a foil pan.

cards.question: When do the guards carry out Rehoboam's bronze shields?

answers.text: Whenever the king enters the house of the LORD
Whenever an enemy army comes near the city
Whenever a new captain takes over the guard

cards.text: Want the rest of Rehoboam's acts? They're in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.

cards.question: True or false: Rehoboam and Jeroboam king of Israel make peace after a few years.

cards.text: After seventeen years on the throne, Rehoboam rests with his fathers and is buried with them in the City of David.

cards.question: Which son reigns in Rehoboam's place?

cards.text: Now Abijam son of Rehoboam becomes king of Judah in the eighteenth year of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and he reigns in Jerusalem three years. His mother's name is Maacah daughter of Abishalom.

cards.question: Which way does Abijam walk?

answers.text: In all the sins of his father
Closer to the LORD than his father
Away from every idol in Judah

cards.question: Abijam's heart was not as fully devoted to the LORD as the heart of his forefather ___.

cards.text: Nevertheless, for the sake of David, the LORD his God gives Abijam a lamp in Jerusalem. Baker, great-grandpa's name is carrying this whole batch.

cards.question: What is the lamp the LORD gives Abijam in Jerusalem?

answers.text: A son to succeed him and make Jerusalem strong
A prophet to speak the LORD's word to him
A victory over Jeroboam king of Israel

cards.text: It's for David's sake, because David did what was right in the eyes of the LORD and didn't turn aside from anything the LORD commanded all his life. Well... ALMOST anything.

cards.question: David never turned aside from the LORD's commands, except in the matter of ___ the Hittite.
True or false: Once Abijam is king, the war between the houses of Rehoboam and Jeroboam finally ends.

cards.text: Abijam's acts are in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah, and then he rests with his fathers and his son Asa reigns in his place. Three years, friend, and I've had dough in the freezer longer than that.
Asa becomes king of Judah in the twentieth year of Jeroboam's reign over Israel, and he reigns in Jerusalem FORTY-ONE years. His dad got three, so that's not a reign, friend, that's a career.

cards.question: Asa's grandmother has a name we heard when his father Abijam took the throne. Who is she?
True or false: Asa does what is right in the eyes of the LORD, as David had done.

cards.text: And Asa doesn't just talk about it. He banishes the male shrine prostitutes from the land, the kind we saw back in Rehoboam's day.

cards.question: True or false: Asa leaves the idols his fathers made standing in the land.

cards.text: Then comes the hard one. His own grandmother Maacah has made a detestable Asherah pole.

cards.question: What does Asa do about his grandmother Maacah?

answers.text: He removes her as queen mother
He lets her keep her place
He sends her away to Egypt

cards.text: Then Asa chops down her pole and burns it in the Kidron Valley. I don't know what the holidays looked like after that, but I bet they were QUIET.

cards.question: True or false: Asa removes the high places too.
The high places stay, but Asa's heart was fully ___ to the LORD all his days.

cards.text: Asa's still on the throne in Judah, and he's still cleaning house. He brings into the house of the LORD the silver and gold and the articles that he and his father had dedicated.
But there's war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel throughout their days. Baasha goes to war against Judah and fortifies Ramah.

cards.question: Baasha fortifies Ramah to keep anyone from leaving or ___ the territory of Asa king of Judah.

cards.text: Asa's boxed in. So he takes all the silver and gold left in the treasuries of the house of the LORD and the royal palace, and he hands it to his servants.

cards.question: Who does Asa send his servants to with all that silver and gold?
Asa asks Ben-hadad king of Aram to break his ___ with Baasha king of Israel.

cards.text: Asa's message says, “See, I have sent you a gift of silver and gold.” Friend, that's not a gift, that's a down payment.

cards.question: True or false: Ben-hadad turns down Asa's silver and gold and stays loyal to Baasha.

cards.text: Ben-hadad sends the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel. They conquer Ijon, Dan, Abel-beth-maacah and the whole land of Naphtali, including Chinnereth.

cards.question: True or false: When Baasha learns his cities are falling, he keeps right on fortifying Ramah.

cards.text: Then King Asa summons all the men of Judah, with NO exceptions. Not one “I'll be there in five” text in the whole kingdom.

cards.question: What do the men of Judah do at Ramah?

answers.text: Carry off its stones and timbers

cards.question: What does King Asa do with Baasha's stones and timbers?

answers.text: Builds a new palace in Jerusalem
Repairs the house of the LORD

cards.text: The rest of Asa's acts, all his might, all his accomplishments and the cities he built, are in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah. Forty-one years, baker, so that book has some PAGES.

cards.question: True or false: Asa stays healthy right to the end of his life.

cards.text: In his old age Asa's feet become diseased. Then he rests with his fathers and is buried with them in the city of his father David.

cards.question: Which son reigns in Asa's place?

findings.problem: The opening card starts with 'Meanwhile' but never says what is happening meanwhile. The baker isn't told that Jeroboam is reigning over Israel at the same time, or that the kingdom has split. Jeroboam then appears with no setup in card 13, and the war between Judah and Israel runs through the whole passage.

rule.text: If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: Most of this stop's choice cards can only be answered by luck. Nothing before them points to the answer: card 2 (Judah provokes the LORD; card 1 gives no hint about Judah's conduct), card 7 (gold shields), card 9 (bronze; card 8 never hints that the replacements are a downgrade), card 11 (when the guards carry the shields), card 13 (no peace with Jeroboam) and card 15 (Abijam, a name never mentioned before). Only cards 4 and 6 can be reasoned out.

rule.text: A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: No card has mentioned Jeroboam or any conflict between Judah and Israel. The baker is asked whether Rehoboam and Jeroboam make peace with nothing to reason from.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: 'Gotta give the guards SOMETHING to carry' gives a reason for why Rehoboam made the bronze shields. The text gives no reason. The line also brings up the guards carrying shields before verse 14:28 is told.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The joke 'No knock, no text, no heads-up in the group chat' puts the modern image into the Bible scene itself, with Shishak not texting. It also suggests the attack came without warning, which the text doesn't say.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The joke 'Not one “I'll be there in five” text in the whole kingdom' blends modern texting into Judah's muster instead of giving a separate everyday comparison.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: 'Then comes the hard one' states as fact that this was hard for Asa. The text doesn't say how Asa felt, and the line isn't marked as Papa Dorin's guess.

rule.text: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The blank asks for 'devoted' in 'fully ___ to the LORD'. Card 3's question already showed the same phrase, 'not as fully devoted to the LORD', so an earlier card gives away this answer.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.
